directions.schema: registering the named message type raises expect_error

cases.name: scalars_full
cases.note: Every scalar type at a boundary or otherwise notable value. Note int64 is an Integer while uint64/fixed64 are Strings, and float widens to doubleValue.

cases.name: scalars_defaults
cases.note: Every field at its default. Implicit presence means all of them are omitted, so the document is empty (§6).

cases.name: doubles_special
cases.note: NaN and the infinities are native Firestore doubles. In REST JSON they are carried as strings because JSON numbers cannot express them.

cases.name: double_from_integer
cases.note: A double or float field must decode from a Firestore Integer, not only from a Double. Nothing in the schema makes this optional: the JavaScript SDK stores an integral double as an integer (§8), so a document written by one language must stay readable by another. Decode-only -- re-encoding yields a Double, which is correct.

cases.name: enums
cases.note: Both encodings in one message: the default name string, and the NUMBER override from the field option.

cases.name: enum_unknown_name
cases.note: A name written by a newer writer must decode to the zero value rather than throw (§4). Decode-only: re-encoding the zero value would omit the field.

cases.name: presence_set
cases.note: Explicit-presence fields set to their default values are still written. This is the case that distinguishes `optional` from an implicit-presence field, and an empty message from an absent one.

cases.name: presence_unset
cases.note: Nothing set, so nothing written.

cases.name: unsigned_boundaries
cases.note: The four boundary values. 2^63 is the one that separates a correct implementation from one that formatted a signed long: it reads back negative in Dart and Java. `zero` and `always` are left out of the input rather than written as "0": an implicit-presence field assigned its default is indistinguishable from an unset one in proto3, and runtimes disagree about whether it serializes, so spelling it out would make this vector language-specific. Both are still 0. `zero` is omitted from the document by §6; `always` carries omit_when_default:false and so is written as "0".

cases.name: unsigned_leading_zeros
cases.note: Canonical form has no leading zeros.

cases.name: unsigned_signed
cases.note: Canonical form has no sign.

cases.name: unsigned_non_digits
cases.note: Decimal digits only.

cases.name: unsigned_overflow
cases.note: 2^64, one past the maximum.

cases.name: unsigned_as_integer_overflow
cases.note: KIND_UNSIGNED_AS_INTEGER must throw rather than write a negative integer.

cases.name: wellknown
cases.note: The timestamp carries sub-microsecond nanos on purpose. The CODEC is exact and must round-trip all nine digits; Firestore itself truncates to microseconds on write, which is a property of the database, not of this encoding (§3.1).

cases.name: latlng_out_of_range
cases.note: Latitude beyond +90. Validated here so the failure names the field, rather than surfacing later as an opaque Firestore write rejection (§3.3).

cases.name: composite_full
cases.note: Nested message, repeated scalar, repeated message, and both map flavours. The second element of `messages` is an empty message, which must encode as an empty mapValue rather than being dropped from the array.

cases.name: composite_empty
cases.note: Empty repeated fields and empty maps are omitted, not written as [] or {} (§6). Contrast with presence_set, where an empty *message* is written.

cases.name: options_skip_and_rename
cases.note: skip:true drops the field; name: overrides the stored key. Encode-only, because `dropped` cannot survive a round trip by design.

cases.name: nesting_depth_20
cases.note: A chain of 20 nested messages puts the innermost map at Firestore's maximum depth of 20. Must encode successfully.

cases.name: nesting_depth_21
cases.note: One level past the limit. The codec must reject this rather than let Firestore refuse the write (§5).

cases.name: schema_int_key_map
cases.note: map<int32, string> must be rejected, not stringified (§5).

cases.name: schema_any_field
cases.note: google.protobuf.Any is not supported (§3.4).

cases.name: schema_struct_field
cases.note: google.protobuf.Struct is not supported (§3.4).

cases.name: duration_negative
cases.note: A negative Duration. seconds and nanos share a sign in protobuf, so -1.5s is seconds=-1, nanos=-500000000. Decoding must split the microsecond count with truncating division and a sign-preserving remainder: a Euclidean modulo yields seconds=-1, nanos=+500000000, which is -0.5s. A negative duration under one second (seconds 0, nanos negative) exercises the same split and is worth a language-local test, but is not a portable vector: Dart's proto3 JSON parser drops the sign when the integer part is zero.

cases.name: oneof_set_default
cases.note: A oneof member set to its default value. Oneof members have explicit presence (§6), so the zero is written, and it must decode back into the oneof: a decoder that assigns the member as a plain property loses the field entirely on runtimes that model oneofs as a tagged union.

cases.name: oneof_set_message
cases.note: A message-typed oneof member, taking the nested-map path through the oneof.

cases.name: int64_jstype_string
cases.note: int64 fields annotated jstype = JS_STRING are still Firestore Integers. protobuf-es generates them as JavaScript strings, and an implementation that passes the value through writes a Firestore String, splitting the field's type across languages (§2.1). The value is 2^53+1, beyond what a JavaScript number can hold exactly.

cases.name: int64_jstype_string_default
cases.note: The default of a JS_STRING int64 is the string "0", which must still count as the default and be omitted (§6). Encode-only: an implicit-presence field assigned its default is indistinguishable from an unset one in proto3, and runtimes disagree about whether it serializes, so the decode comparison would be language-specific (see unsigned_boundaries).

cases.name: enum_unknown_number
cases.note: An enum number with no declared name, as relayed from a newer writer, has no representation under the name encoding (§4). Writing the raw integer would mix types on a String field; writing a synthetic name would decode to zero and destroy the newer writer's value. Both are silent, so the codec throws. Under enum_as: NUMBER the integer is representable and is written.

requirements.open_enum_values: the runtime can hold an enum number that is not declared in the schema (Java, protobuf-es). A runtime with closed enums (Dart) cannot construct the input and may skip the case; it is conformant by construction.
